name: Fraction, decimal and percentage
description:
Fraction: a number written as a numerator divided by a denominator, such as 3/4.
Decimal: a number written with a decimal point, such as 0.75.
Percentage: a number of hundredths, so 75 % means 75 out of 100.

name: Convert between fractions, decimals and percentages
description: convert a number between fraction, decimal and percentage form in every direction, including percentages above 100 % and below 1 %

name: Calculate a percentage of an amount
description: calculate a given percentage of an amount, by hand for simple percentages and with a calculator for the rest

name: Find what percentage one amount is of another
description: calculate what percentage a part is of a whole, and say clearly which quantity is the whole

name: Percentage change
description: Percentage change: the size of a change given as a percentage of the value before the change.

name: Calculate a percentage change
description: calculate the percentage increase or decrease from one value to another, using the value before the change as the base

name: Percentage point
description: Percentage point: the unit for the difference between two percentages, so a rise from 20 % to 25 % is 5 percentage points.

name: Explain the difference between percentage points and per cent
description: calculate both the change in percentage points and the percentage change for the same situation, and explain why the two numbers differ

name: Power
description: Power: a product of equal factors written with an exponent, so 1.05^3 means 1.05 · 1.05 · 1.05.

name: Growth factor
description: Growth factor: the number a value is multiplied by to give the value after a percentage change, such as 1.25 for an increase of 25 % and 0.75 for a decrease of 25 %.

name: Calculate a new value with a growth factor
description: find the growth factor for a given percentage increase or decrease, use it to calculate the new value, and find the percentage change from a given growth factor

name: Find the value before a percentage change
description: calculate the original value when the new value and the percentage change are known, by dividing by the growth factor

name: Calculate repeated percentage changes
description: calculate the result of several percentage changes in a row, including changes of different sizes, and explain why an increase of 10 % followed by a decrease of 10 % does not give the starting value

name: Linear and exponential growth
description:
Linear growth: growth in which a quantity changes by the same amount in each period.
Exponential growth: growth in which a quantity changes by the same percentage in each period, so it is multiplied by the same growth factor each time; with a growth factor below 1 it is called exponential decay.

name: Model exponential growth with a formula
description: write an expression of the form start value · growth factor^n for a practical situation, use it to calculate values, and say what n stands for

name: Explain the difference between linear and exponential growth
description: decide from a description or a table whether a situation shows linear or exponential growth, and explain what makes the difference

name: Write formulas in a spreadsheet
description: write a formula that refers to other cells, copy it down a column so that it works in every row, and lock a cell reference with $ where it must not move

name: Model growth in a spreadsheet
description: set up a spreadsheet that calculates a value period by period with a growth factor, and use it or a graph to find when the value passes a given level

name: Price index
description: Price index: a number that shows the price level in a given year compared with a base year, where the base year is set to 100; in Norway the usual one is the consumer price index (konsumprisindeks, KPI).

name: Calculate with a price index
description: use index numbers to convert a price or an amount from one year to another, and find the percentage price change between two years

name: Value of the krone
description: Value of the krone (kroneverdi): how much one krone buys compared with the base year, calculated as 100 divided by the price index.

name: Real wage and purchasing power
description:
Purchasing power: how much a sum of money can buy.
Real wage (reallønn): the wage as paid, converted to the price level of a chosen base year so that wages from different years can be compared.

name: Calculate the value of the krone and real wage
description: calculate the value of the krone for a given year, and calculate the real wage from a wage and the price index

name: Compare purchasing power across years
description: decide whether purchasing power has risen or fallen between two years by comparing real wages, and explain the conclusion in words

name: Gross and net income
description:
Gross income: pay before tax and other deductions.
Net income: the amount paid out after tax and other deductions.

name: Tax card and withholding tax
description:
Tax card (skattekort): the notice from the Tax Administration that tells the employer how much tax to deduct.
Withholding tax (forskuddstrekk): tax deducted from each payment of wages according to the tax card, either as a fixed percentage or from a tax table.

name: Calculate gross pay
description: calculate gross pay from hourly wage, hours worked and overtime supplements given as percentages

name: Calculate net pay
description: calculate net pay from gross pay, withholding tax by percentage or tax table, and other deductions such as pension contributions or union fees, and check the figures on a payslip

name: Make a budget
description: set up a monthly budget with income and expenses in a spreadsheet, find out whether it balances, and suggest realistic changes if it does not

name: Interest and interest rate
description:
Interest: what you pay for borrowing money, or are paid for saving it.
Interest rate: the interest for one year given as a percentage of the amount.

name: Calculate savings with compound interest
description: calculate how an amount grows over several years when interest is added each year, using a growth factor and a power

name: Instalment, serial loan and annuity loan
description:
Instalment (avdrag): the part of a loan payment that pays down the debt itself.
Serial loan (serielån): a loan where the instalment is the same every period, so the payment falls as the interest falls.
Annuity loan (annuitetslån): a loan where the total payment is the same every period, so the interest share falls and the instalment share rises.

name: Set up a repayment plan for a loan
description: set up a repayment plan in a spreadsheet for a serial loan and for an annuity loan, and find the total interest paid over the loan period

name: Effective interest rate
description: Effective interest rate: the total yearly cost of a loan including fees, given as a percentage of the amount borrowed; it is the figure to use when comparing loans.

name: Compare loan offers
description: compare two or more loan offers using effective interest rate, total cost and monthly payment, and argue for which one suits a given situation

name: Credit card
description: Credit card: a card that lets you borrow up to a set limit, usually with an interest-free period followed by a high interest rate on any amount not paid back.

name: Evaluate the consequences of loans and credit cards
description: calculate what a credit card debt or consumer loan grows to over time when only small payments are made, and use the numbers to argue for or against a financial choice

name: Equation and solution
description:
Equation: a statement that two expressions are equal, containing at least one unknown.
Solution: a value of the unknown that makes both sides equal.

name: Solve a linear equation
description: solve a linear equation by doing the same operation on both sides, including equations with brackets and fractions, and check the answer by substituting it back

name: Proportional quantities
description: Proportional quantities: two quantities whose ratio is always the same, so that doubling one doubles the other.

name: Solve a proportion
description: set up an equation of the form a/b = x/d from a practical situation and solve it

name: Set up an equation from a text
description: translate a practical problem into an equation, solve it, and answer in a sentence with the correct unit

name: System of equations
description: System of equations: two or more equations with the same unknowns that must be true at the same time; its solution is the set of values that makes every equation true.

name: Solve a system of equations by calculation
description: solve a system of two linear equations with two unknowns by substitution or elimination, and check the solution in both equations

name: Coordinate system
description: Coordinate system: two number lines at right angles, the x-axis and the y-axis, where each point is given by a pair (x, y).

name: Slope and constant term
description:
Slope: how much y changes when x increases by 1 on a straight line y = ax + b; it is the number a.
Constant term: the value of y when x is 0, where the line crosses the y-axis; it is the number b.

name: Solve a system of equations graphically
description: draw both lines of a system of two linear equations with a digital tool, read off the point where they cross, and explain why that point is the solution

name: Set up a system of equations from a text
description: translate a practical problem with two unknowns into a system of equations, solve it, and answer in words

name: Inequality
description: Inequality: a statement that one expression is greater than or less than another, written with <, >, ≤ or ≥; its solution is usually a whole range of values.

name: Solve a linear inequality
description: solve a linear inequality, turning the inequality sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number, and show the solution on a number line

name: Compare strategies for solving equations
description: solve the same equation or system in more than one way, such as by calculation, from a graph, by trial and improvement or with a digital tool, and argue for which method suits which problem

name: Categorical and numerical data
description:
Categorical data: observations that are categories, such as favourite sport.
Numerical data: observations that are numbers from counting or measuring, such as height.

name: Frequency
description:
Frequency: how many times a value occurs in a dataset.
Relative frequency: the frequency as a fraction or percentage of all the observations.
Cumulative frequency: the sum of the frequencies up to and including a value.

name: Make a frequency table
description: sort raw data into a frequency table with columns for frequency, relative frequency and cumulative frequency

name: Present data in a suitable diagram
description: draw bar charts, pie charts and line charts by hand and with a digital tool, and choose a type that suits the data and the message

name: Class interval and class midpoint
description:
Class interval: a range of values that observations are grouped into, such as 10-20 minutes.
Class midpoint: the value halfway between the ends of a class interval.

name: Group data and draw a histogram
description: group numerical data into class intervals, make a frequency table for the groups, and draw a histogram

name: Mean, median and mode
description:
Mean: the sum of all the observations divided by the number of observations.
Median: the middle value when the observations are sorted, or the mean of the two middle values.
Mode: the value that occurs most often.

name: Calculate mean, median and mode
description: calculate mean, median and mode from a list of observations and from a frequency table

name: Estimate the mean of grouped data
description: estimate the mean of grouped data using class midpoints, and explain why the result is only an estimate

name: Outlier
description: Outlier: an observation that lies far from the rest of the data.

name: Range and interquartile range
description:
Range: the difference between the largest and the smallest observation.
Quartiles: the three values that split the sorted observations into four equal parts; the middle one is the median.
Interquartile range: the difference between the upper and the lower quartile.

name: Calculate range and interquartile range
description: find the range, the quartiles and the interquartile range of a dataset

name: Standard deviation
description: Standard deviation: a measure of how far the observations typically lie from the mean; a small value means the data are gathered close to the mean.

name: Find the standard deviation with a digital tool
description: find the standard deviation of a dataset with a spreadsheet or other digital tool, and explain what a large or small value says about the data

name: Choose suitable measures for a dataset
description: decide which measure of central tendency and which measure of spread best describe a given dataset, including when it has outliers, and justify the choice

name: Analyse and present a real dataset
description: find or collect a dataset from the local community or the media, summarise it with suitable measures and diagrams, and present the conclusions together with their limitations

name: Evaluate statistics in the media
description: spot misleading statistics in the media, such as cut axes, percentages without a stated base, percentage points confused with per cent, or a mean pulled by outliers, and explain what an honest presentation would show

name: Convert between units
description: convert between units of length, area and volume, including between litres and cubic decimetres

name: Perimeter and area
description:
Perimeter: the length of the boundary around a figure.
Area: the size of the surface a figure covers, measured in square units.

name: Calculate perimeter and area
description: calculate the perimeter and area of rectangles, triangles, parallelograms, trapeziums, circles and figures made up of these

name: Volume and surface area
description:
Volume: the amount of space a solid takes up, measured in cubic units.
Surface area: the total area of all the faces of a solid.

name: Calculate volume and surface area
description: calculate the volume and surface area of prisms and cylinders, and the volume of pyramids, cones and spheres, giving the answer in a suitable unit

name: Pythagoras' theorem
description: Pythagoras' theorem: in a right-angled triangle, the square of the longest side (the hypotenuse) equals the sum of the squares of the two other sides.

name: Use Pythagoras' theorem
description: calculate an unknown side in a right-angled triangle, and use the theorem to check whether a corner is square in practical work

name: Similar figures
description: Similar figures: figures with the same shape, where corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same ratio.

name: Decide whether two figures are similar
description: decide whether two triangles or other figures are similar, and pair up their corresponding sides and angles

name: Calculate sides in similar figures
description: calculate an unknown side in similar figures by setting up a proportion, including in practical situations such as finding the height of a tree from its shadow

name: Scale
description: Scale: the ratio between a length on a map or drawing and the corresponding length in reality, written for example as 1 : 50 000.

name: Calculate with scale
description: convert between lengths on a map or drawing and lengths in reality, and find the scale from a pair of corresponding lengths

name: Make a scale drawing
description: choose a suitable scale and make an accurate scale drawing of a real object or room

name: Explain how area and volume change when a figure is enlarged
description: explain and use the fact that when all lengths are multiplied by k, the area is multiplied by k^2 and the volume by k^3

name: Solve a practical geometry problem
description: plan and carry out a practical task, such as working out the materials for a building or garden project, using scale, area, volume and Pythagoras' theorem, and judge whether the answer is reasonable
